With about four hours before boarding, you've got plenty of room to properly rest. The Snooze Lounge in T1 is free, with reclining chairs, dim lighting and small privacy screens. It's first-come-first-served, and it's usually calmest after 11pm, so it may be busier right now. For a real lie-down, Crowne Plaza Changi Airport is connected directly to T1 and offers day-use rooms, so you could sleep in peace. Availability and rates can vary, so check at the front desk.

If you'd rather have a gentler wind-down, the Cactus Garden is a calm open-air spot on the T1 rooftop, and the dnata Lounge is spacious and comfortable if you have Priority Pass access.

If you just want a quick snack, Old Chang Kee's curry puffs are the classic local grab, though it closes at 9 pm so you'd want to be quick tonight.

results.message: Happy to help with restless little ones! Start at the Butterfly Garden (about 15 min), where around 1,000 butterflies flutter in a glass conservatory. Go early, before the tour groups arrive. Then Kaboom, right nearby, has separate toddler and junior play sections, and the free Entertainment Deck has walk-in consoles, music booths and a cinema, so the kids can burn off energy for 45 min or so. It's peak dinner time, so food queues (Sushi Tei's conveyor belt is a kid-friendly option) could add 10-20 min, but with about 165 usable minutes you have room, and I'd keep a 15 min buffer at the end for your gate.
